issues.description: Field mismatch: In the Solution's Person class the field 'id' is declared as 'Integer' while the same class's getter and setter use 'Long' and the PersonRepository is parameterized with 'Long'. The Template's Person class declares 'id' as 'Long'. Specifically: solution_repository/src/.../model/Person.java declares 'private Integer id;' but its methods 'public Long getId()' and 'public void setId(Long id)' use Long. The repository interface (solution_repository/src/.../repository/PersonRepository.java) and the template model (template_repository/src/.../model/Person.java) consistently use Long. This inconsistency will cause compilation errors and confusion for students when compiling or using JpaRepository<Person, Long].
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Person.id type consistent across artifacts. Change the Solution's Person.id field from 'Integer' to 'Long' so it matches the getter/setter signatures and the JpaRepository<Person, Long>. Verify getter/setter and repository generics are all 'Long' (or change all to Integer, but prefer Long to match the template and repository). Rebuild to ensure no further type mismatches.

issues.description: The Person entity identifier 'id' is represented with inconsistent Java types across artifacts: the template's Person class declares the field as 'private Long id' (template: src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java) and the repository is parameterized as JpaRepository<Person, Long> (template: src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/repository/PersonRepository.java), but the solution's Person class declares the field as 'private Integer id' while its getter and setter use Long. This mixes Integer and Long for the same conceptual identifier. Students reading the exercise see the repository and template use Long, but the solution's field type differs (and the solution's accessor types conflict with its field), which creates confusion about the expected identifier type and may cause compile/runtime or persistence mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the Person identifier type across all artifacts. Change the solution repository's Person class to declare the id field as 'private Long id' and ensure the getter and setter signatures use Long (public Long getId(), public void setId(Long id)) so the entity type matches JpaRepository<Person, Long> and the template code. Verify the database mapping (BIGINT) remains consistent.
